macro_catalyst: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and director on Sun Nov 22 (announced pre-open Nov 23), 11 days after his Nov 12 resignation. Board cited satisfaction with his 'candor and ability to lead NVIDIA' and said US-government input left it confident his return 'poses no national security risk'. Colette Kress reverts from interim CEO to CFO. NVDA +31% premarket. This reversed the AI-complex crash his exit triggered: QQQ fell 5.67% on Nov 20 and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026 on a trillion-dollar weekly wipeout. Caveats: on the Nov 17 earnings call chair Harvey Jones said the board 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen'; Trump publicly pressured the board over the weekend; and a committee of independent directors is still investigating reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

gappers.catalyst: Huang's reinstatement as NVDA CEO triggers violent dip-buying across neocloud/AI-infra; NBIS bounces off a $73.52 52-week low.
headlines: NVIDIA board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, stock jumps 30% premarket (Stock Analysis)
Why Are Neocloud Stocks CoreWeave, IREN, and Nebius Rallying in Premarket Today, November 23? (TipRanks)
Michael Burry says he 'tried to warn' investors that Nvidia, CoreWeave and Nebius were headed for trouble (Business Insider)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius is an AI-infrastructure 'neocloud' renting large-scale GPU clusters. It had been the epicentre of the AI de-rating: Q3 (Nov 12) beat on revenue but guided $40B of 2027 capex, far above consensus, and the stock lost roughly 64% from its high as analysts cut targets on construction delays and cost concerns. Huang's Nov 12 exit removed the sector's main sponsor and credit backstop, and NBIS fell a further 16.11% on Nov 20 to $81.31. His unanimous reinstatement, announced pre-open today, restores that sponsor, and NBIS is marked at $105.15 (+29.32%).
gappers.why: Mechanism is sponsor-risk reversal, not fundamentals. Neocloud equity is a levered call on Nvidia's willingness to keep supplying and financing GPU capacity; Huang's departure repriced that counterparty risk, and his return un-prices it. Nothing about Nebius's own $40B capex plan, 193x P/E or construction delays changed over the weekend.
gappers.impact: Reads as a sharp relief retrace inside a broken downtrend, not a sustainable breakout. Even at +29% the stock sits ~65% below its $299.86 52-week high and has not reclaimed its Nov 19 close of $96.92 by much. Sector read-through is total rather than specific: CRWV +27.9%, IREN rallying on the identical driver, which confirms this is a one-factor sector trade and that NBIS offers no idiosyncratic edge. Gap is ~22pts of alpha over QQQ, the widest on the list, which cuts both ways: largest bounce also means largest unwind if the Huang story is walked back.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A reinstatement that reverses a stated board position from six days earlier, delivered under public political pressure and with a foreign-intelligence investigation still open, is headline-driven and reversible, not a structural guidance or contract reset.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - the account holds zero positions and 0/3 weekly trades are used, so the real cost is the week's scarce trade slots and the risk budget. The binding problem is the R:R gate, not the cap: the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at ~$94.6, inside Friday's $80.67-$94.04 range, so ordinary gap-fill noise stops it out, and clearing 2:1 needs +59% to ~$167 - implausible in days. A stop placed outside Friday's range instead implies ~23% risk, over twice the 1.0%-of-equity ATR sizing allowance. Taking it would also consume the beta slot that CRWV (rank 2, same single driver, correlation far above the 0.75 gate) competes for; the two are one trade, not two.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - fails R:R gate at any sane stop distance; chasing a +29% gap into a reversible headline.

gappers.catalyst: Same Huang-reinstatement neocloud bounce, plus Citizens JMP reiterating Buy with a $180 target and Cathie Wood disclosed buying $24.7M.
headlines: NVIDIA board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, stock jumps 30% premarket (Stock Analysis)
CoreWeave Stock Forecast: Citizens Raises Estimates on Strong AI Demand and Higher GPU Pricing (TipRanks)
CRWV falls toward its $40 IPO price as a $66.2B debt load worries investors (TipRanks)
gappers.catalyst_detail: CoreWeave is the largest listed neocloud, with TTM revenue of $9.89B (+129.6%) against a $66.2B debt load. Last week it fell toward its $40 IPO price as that leverage drew scrutiny; it dropped 12.02% on Nov 20 to $39.51 as Anthropic-IPO optimism faded. Over the prior days insiders and sponsors leaned in: Huang's foundation pledged $350M to rent CoreWeave compute, co-founder Brian Venturo bought $30M face value of its bonds, and Citizens JMP reiterated Buy at a $180 target. With Huang reinstated it is marked at $50.55 (+27.94%).
gappers.why: Leverage plus sponsor risk. A $66.2B debt load against negative free cash flow makes the equity a levered bet on continued AI capex and on cheap financing; Huang's exit widened its credit spread and his return narrows it. The Citizens note and Wood's buying are confirmation of an existing bull case, not new information, and were already public before Friday's decline.
gappers.impact: Most likely a credit-driven relief bounce rather than a trend change. The stock is only ~$10 above its IPO price with market cap still down 41.1%, and the debt concern that drove the selloff is untouched. Read-through is identical to NBIS and IREN, so it supplies no diversification: these are the same trade. The $350M Huang-foundation compute pledge and the insider bond buy are mildly supportive and specific to CRWV, which marginally distinguishes it from NBIS.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The driver is the same reversible CEO headline; the structural overhang - $66.2B of debt needing refinancing - is unchanged and is what will set the medium-term path.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Competes directly with NBIS for one AI-infra slot; the correlation gate blocks holding both, and entering either forfeits the ability to add the other. Against zero open positions the cost is the trade slot, not a displaced holding. R:R also fails: a 10% trail at ~$45.5 is inside Friday's trading range and barely above the $40 IPO shelf, while 2:1 requires ~$78 (+55%). Highlighting the scan defect matters more than the trade here - this name was ranked 20th at +6.0% on the delayed feed and would have been dropped from the top-10 entirely.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - fails R:R; same single factor as NBIS, unresolved leverage.

gappers.catalyst: No equity-specific driver; Ethereum-treasury beta. Reported $11.1B of total crypto, cash and 'moonshot' holdings as of Nov 22 3:00pm ET.
headlines: Bitmine Immersion reports total holdings $11.1B (TheFly)
Bitmine Immersion Technologies announces ETH holdings reach 6.07 million tokens (OTC Markets, Nov 20)
B. Riley lowers price target to $27 from $34, keeps Buy
gappers.catalyst_detail: BitMine is an Ethereum treasury vehicle: an $8.13B market cap wrapped around ~6.08M ETH, about 4.97% of total supply as of Nov 15. Its only fresh disclosure is a routine holdings update posted this morning putting total crypto, cash and 'moonshots' at $11.1B as of Nov 22 3:00pm ET. There is no corporate catalyst. The stock fell 13.87% on Nov 20 to $12.98 and is marked at $15.03 (+15.79%). B. Riley cut its target to $27 from $34 while keeping Buy, and the shares are down ~52% over twelve months.
gappers.why: Pure risk-asset beta transmitted through a leveraged NAV wrapper. Equity trades at a premium or discount to its ETH stack, so a risk-on reversal moves the stock more than the underlying coin. The $11.1B figure is a weekend snapshot that confirms the holdings rather than changing them, and at $8.13B market cap against $11.1B of assets the stock is marked below its own stated NAV.
gappers.impact: Likely to mean-revert with crypto rather than hold a gain, and is the one name here whose driver is not the Huang headline - it is a different factor that happens to be moving the same way, which is worth noting for correlation purposes. The NAV discount is the only genuinely interesting feature and is a valuation observation, not a catalyst. Sustainability depends entirely on ETH, which this scan did not price, so the read is low-confidence.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A holdings-snapshot press release is not a structural catalyst, and crypto-proxy equities have no durable thesis independent of the coin; the sector-rotation table gives no phase in which an ETH treasury wrapper is a favoured sector.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Would displace nothing held, but spends a trade slot on an undiversifiable crypto-beta proxy while the account already has no equity exposure at all - a poor first position when the mandate is to beat the S&P. R:R is marginally the least bad on the list because the NAV floor gives the stop some logic, but a 10% trail at ~$13.5 still sits inside Friday's range, and 2:1 needs ~$24 (+60%), near B. Riley's $27 target - achievable only on a large ETH move this scan has no read on. Taking it would also mean passing on the better-sponsored AI-infra names, though those fail their own gates.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - no catalyst, undiversifiable single-factor crypto beta, R:R unmet.

With no company news the move is entirely explained by the index gap and by defense/drone names re-rating with risk appetite. A $2.22B cap on $331M of revenue means the price is carried by sentiment and the growth narrative, which is exactly what mechanically reverses hardest in both directions.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day beta spike likely to fade. It is the lowest-priced name in the top five at $4.32, so percentage moves overstate how much is really happening, and even after +14.8% it has not recovered Friday's loss plus the preceding week's. Read-through is the broad defense/drone complex, with UMAC (rank 10) moving on the same non-catalyst, so again no idiosyncratic signal. The $16.68 consensus target against a $4.32 price is a 344% implied upside that should be treated as stale rather than as a forecast.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No catalyst at all, so there is nothing structural to carry; the move is index beta on a sub-$5 stock and the strategy's own rule is to pass when the entry checklist's catalyst line is empty.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing, but would spend one of three weekly trades on the thinnest thesis in the top five - strictly worse than the ranks 1-2 setups on sponsorship even though all of them fail. Sub-$5 price means the 10% trail sits ~$0.43 away, well inside the stock's daily range, so it would almost certainly be stopped for a full loss before any 2:1 target near $6.20 could be reached. Defense exposure is better taken through RKLB (rank 7) on quality if the sector is wanted at all.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - no documented catalyst, fails the entry checklist outright.

gappers.why: Index beta plus sector sympathy, with no stock-specific mechanism. Pre-revenue-scale space names carry very high beta to risk appetite, so a 7% index gap mechanically produces a low-double-digit move in them. Its genuine catalysts are mission milestones and contract awards, none of which is dated to today.
gappers.impact: Lowest-conviction read in the top five: thinnest volume, oldest news, and a move fully accounted for by the tape. A one-day headline spike with nothing to hold it, and the whole space complex moving together (RKLB +13.8%, RDW +13.3%, BKSY, PL) confirms there is no name-specific signal. If anything the sympathy is a reason for caution - buying the laggard of a correlated group on a beta day is how the strategy's 'exit a sector after 2 failed trades' rule gets triggered.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A move with no catalyst and no news for a week has nothing structural behind it; Technology/Industrials being an early-cycle favoured sector does not convert a beta spike into a thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace, but it is the clearest 'do not spend a slot here' on the list: identical driver to three other space names on the scan, so it adds correlation without adding edge, and taking it would forfeit a trade slot that a genuinely catalysed setup later this week could use.
